domain_hypothesis.reasoning: The dataset contains columns representing employee demographics (Age, Gender, MaritalStatus), performance and tenure metrics (YearsAtCompany, PerformanceRating, YearsSinceLastPromotion), job specifics (Department, JobRole, JobLevel), and critical HR target outcomes like Attrition.

kpi_specs.name: Overall Attrition Rate
kpi_specs.description: The percentage of employees who have left the company (where Attrition is 'Yes'). This is a primary metric for overall organizational health and retention performance.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN Attrition = 'Yes' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS attrition_rate_pct FROM data
kpi_specs.reasoning: As a critical high-level organizational metric, a card visual provides an immediate and clear snapshot of the company's retention performance.

kpi_specs.name: Average Monthly Income by Department
kpi_specs.description: The average monthly salary of employees grouped by department, helping identify resource allocation and payroll distribution across major business units.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT Department, ROUND(AVG(MonthlyIncome), 2) AS avg_monthly_income FROM data GROUP BY Department ORDER BY avg_monthly_income DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: A bar chart is ideal for comparing aggregate salary metrics across the three discrete departments present in the dataset.

kpi_specs.name: Attrition Rate by Job Role
kpi_specs.description: The percentage of attrition analyzed by job role, highlighting which specific roles are experiencing the highest turnover.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT JobRole, COUNT(*) AS total_employees, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN Attrition = 'Yes' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS attrition_rate_pct FROM data GROUP BY JobRole ORDER BY attrition_rate_pct DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: Comparing attrition rates across 9 distinct job roles is best suited to a bar chart to easily highlight and rank high-risk departments.

kpi_specs.name: Employee Sentiment Profile by Job Role
kpi_specs.description: A comprehensive breakdown of key satisfaction and quality-of-life scores (Job Satisfaction, Work-Life Balance, and Environment Satisfaction) across various roles.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT JobRole, ROUND(AVG(JobSatisfaction), 2) AS avg_job_satisfaction, ROUND(AVG(WorkLifeBalance), 2) AS avg_work_life_balance, ROUND(AVG(EnvironmentSatisfaction), 2) AS avg_env_satisfaction FROM data GROUP BY JobRole ORDER BY avg_job_satisfaction DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: A table is the most suitable visual for multi-column comparisons of numerical survey averages grouped by a dimensional breakdown like Job Role.

kpi_specs.name: Attrition Risk by Tenure
kpi_specs.description: The trend of employee attrition rate calculated over different tenures (Years at Company), identifying critical points in an employee's lifecycle where they are most likely to leave.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT YearsAtCompany, COUNT(*) AS headcount, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN Attrition = 'Yes' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS attrition_rate_pct FROM data GROUP BY YearsAtCompany ORDER BY YearsAtCompany ASC
kpi_specs.reasoning: Tenure (YearsAtCompany) represents continuous, ordered time-like segments, making a line chart the optimal choice for visualizing the trajectory of attrition risk over an employee's career span.
